hint: Hover or tap a part of the diagram.

parts.title: Without shared infrastructure
parts.body: Every program maintains its own scripts: one for BirdNET, one for Perch, one to copy audio, one to submit jobs, spreadsheets of labels, and folders like results_v2_final. They depend on each other in ways nobody wrote down.

parts.title: Inference
parts.body: Runs any model the same way and writes scores, detections and embeddings in one standard format. Adding a model means one small adapter, not a new pipeline.

parts.title: Comparison
parts.body: Tests models against expert labels and picks the clips experts should label next, so labelling effort goes where it improves models most.

parts.title: Fine-tuning
parts.body: Trains a small classifier head on a backbone model using the program's own labels, to do better on local species.

parts.title: Catalog port
parts.body: Turns a selection into a list of recordings: from SoundHub, or simply a folder layout.

parts.title: Storage port
parts.body: Reads and writes audio and results, on Amazon S3 or a lab server.

parts.title: Compute port
parts.body: Runs the work on SageMaker, a Slurm cluster, or a laptop.

parts.title: Inference models port
parts.body: Connects the core to model-specific code: BirdNET, Perch, the Spotted Owl model, or a fine-tuned head.

parts.title: Governance port
parts.body: Checks whether a use is permitted and stamps results with their provenance.

parts.title: Labeling tools
parts.body: Outside the core. Experts listen to the clips comparison picks, in SoundHub or JupyterBioacoustics, and their labels come back to fine-tuning.

parts.title: The new head joins the models
parts.body: A fine-tuned head is registered as another model, so it runs through inference like BirdNET or Perch.
